claims.text: A high-temperature-stable self-lubricating nanocomposite coating on CoCrFeNi will generate a robust, adaptive tribofilm during sliding.
The coating-generated tribofilm will remain effective from room temperature to 800 °C.
The coating-generated tribofilm will minimize friction throughout the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The coating-generated tribofilm will minimize wear throughout the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
A PVD-deposited nanocomposite containing a high-temperature-stable lubricious phase can serve as the proposed intervention.
Sliding contact will cause the engineered coating to generate and preserve an adaptive lubricious tribofilm.
Persistence of the tribofilm will minimize metal-to-metal contact as temperature rises.
High-temperature stability of the coating will keep its lubricious constituents active.
At lower temperatures, the coating will reduce direct-contact friction.
At high temperatures, the coating will form oxidation-resistant phases.
The high-temperature phases will maintain low friction through load transfer.
The high-temperature phases will reduce wear by minimizing abrasive interactions.
Coated CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than uncoated CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
Coated CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than uncoated CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
The coating's improvement will be especially pronounced near 800 °C.
The expected improvement is limited to moderate loads and sliding speeds.
Extreme loads or highly corrosive environments may degrade the coating's performance.
The degree of friction and wear improvement depends on coating formulation, microstructure, and long-term durability.
